cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic describes how the four candidate sets are represented in the fused four-view patient geometry. The four sets are unequal in size (39, 31, 20, 13 patients). Within-set affinity is uniformly high and similar across sets (about 0.0094–0.0101), and between-set affinity across the nearest boundaries is only slightly lower (about 0.00903–0.00908). The narrow margin between within-set and between-set affinity indicates that the current set boundaries are not sharply separated in this fused geometry; the closest pair by between-set affinity is K4_C0002–K4_C0004, but the spread across all listed pairs is small, so this is a pair-review entry point rather than a separation result. Internally, each set's eigengap profile is dominated by the leading gap at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k=1 for all four sets), with subsequent gaps two to three orders of magnitude smaller. This means the internal spectral structure of each set is dominated by the single-cluster resolution and does not, at this screening level, indicate a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision. cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0001 (n=39) versus the heterogeneous rest (n=64), the four-view geometry shows only weak representation of the current membership. In each modality's native distance geometry the within-label and between-label mean distances are nearly identical, and the corresponding silhouettes are near zero for CT (0.003) and WSI (0.003), modest for RNA (0.063), and largest but still limited for WXS (0.090). This means the current K4_C0001 boundary is not sharply expressed in any single modality's native geometry. The global geometry concordance between modality pairs is also low to modest (GRV 0.092-0.198), with the strongest shared structure between WSI and RNA and between CT and WSI, and the weakest between CT and RNA and between WSI and WXS. The permutation results indicate that the patient correspondence between some modality pairs (CT-WSI, RNA-WXS, WSI-RNA) is unlikely under exchangeability, while others (CT-RNA, WSI-WXS, CT-WXS) are not distinguishable from exchangeable correspondence; these p-values are not action gates. Importantly, the low GRV values do not establish that the views disagree on a boundary, and the modest GRV values do not establish that the views support the same boundary; the tool does not recluster, so these measurements describe geometry similarity and current-label alignment rather than shared subtype boundaries. Taken together, K4_C0001 is weakly separated from the rest in every native modality geometry, and the four views share only limited global patient geometry.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0001 (n=39) versus the heterogeneous rest (n=64), the ranked enrichment analysis is estimable and yields a coherent biological phenotype dominated by down-regulation of oxidative phosphorylation (NES -2.025, FDR 0.001), complement (NES -1.942), allograft rejection (NES -1.940), interferon alpha (NES -1.907) and gamma (NES -1.872) responses, and IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling (NES -1.830), all at FDR 0.001. A broader set of metabolic, inflammatory, EMT, coagulation, and proliferation-related pathways is also down-regulated at FDR between roughly 0.002 and 0.11. The leading-edge gene lists show that these are multi-gene coordinated programs: the OXPHOS leading edge is rich in respiratory-chain and TCA-cycle genes, and the interferon leading edges include HLA and antigen-presentation genes. Up-regulation is limited to angiogenesis (NES 1.321, FDR 0.086) and UV-response-DN (NES 1.272, FDR 0.098), neither of which reaches FDR below 0.05. Because the rest group is a mixture of the other three candidate sets, the contrast describes how K4_C0001 differs from a composite background rather than from any single alternative set, and the direction of enrichment is relative to the target-versus-rest Wald-statistic ranking. The overall pattern is a coherent, multi-pathway phenotype with a strong down-regulated immune-metabolic axis and weaker up-regulated angiogenic signal.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0001 (n=39) versus the rest (n=64), the confounder association analysis covers tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT scanner model, CT reconstruction kernel, and the continuous factors slice thickness, pixel spacing, z-spacing, and study year. All other factors show small effect sizes (Cramer's V 0.118-0.187; epsilon-squared 0.0-0.017) and are not significant after correction. Because the analysis is a set-versus-rest contrast, the rest group is a mixture of the other three candidate sets, and the association tests describe how K4_C0001 differs from that composite background. Nonsignificance for the remaining factors does not establish absence of confounding, and the nominal tissue-site and manufacturer signals warrant attention as potential contributors to the geometry.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0003 (n=20) versus the heterogeneous rest (n=83), the ranked enrichment analysis is estimable and yields a coherent immune-activated phenotype dominated by up-regulation of allograft rejection (NES 2.816, FDR 0.001), interferon gamma (NES 2.410), interferon alpha (NES 2.336), IL6-JAK-STAT3 (NES 2.327), inflammatory response (NES 1.977), and complement (NES 1.848), all at FDR 0.001. Additional up-regulated pathways include coagulation, DNA repair, EMT, myogenesis, MYC targets V2, IL2-STAT5, apoptosis, ROS, and apical junction, mostly at FDR between 0.04 and 0.10. The leading-edge gene lists show coordinated HLA, antigen-presentation, T-cell, chemokine, and interferon-stimulated programs. Down-regulated pathways include UV-response-DN (NES -2.062, FDR 0.001), protein secretion (NES -1.961, FDR 0.001), androgen response (NES -1.863, FDR 0.001), fatty-acid metabolism (NES -1.655, FDR 0.008), bile-acid metabolism (NES -1.619, FDR 0.009), and heme metabolism (NES -1.593, FDR 0.011). Because the rest group is a mixture of the other three candidate sets, the contrast describes how K4_C0003 differs from a composite background rather than from any single alternative set. The overall pattern is a coherent, multi-pathway immune/inflammatory activation phenotype with down-regulated metabolic and secretory programs.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0003 (n=20) versus the rest (n=83), the confounder association analysis shows a strong and significant tissue source site association (Cramer's V 0.443, q=0.009), with CJ overrepresented and B0, B8, and BP underrepresented in K4_C0003. CT phase (Cramer's V 0.292, q=0.0585) is nominally significant but not after correction. CT manufacturer (Cramer's V 0.120, q=0.364), scanner model (Cramer's V 0.058, q=0.659), reconstruction kernel (Cramer's V 0.0, q=0.855), pixel spacing (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.904), and study year (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.855) show no significant association. These associations indicate that K4_C0003 differs from the rest in site and some CT acquisition characteristics; this is a location association and not proof of technical artifact or causation, but the significant site and spacing associations mean that technical and site factors could plausibly account for part of the geometry for this set. Because the analysis is a set-versus-rest contrast, the rest group is a mixture of the other three candidate sets.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0003 (n=20) versus the heterogeneous rest (n=83), the WXS mutation enrichment analysis is estimable across 3,583 genes. The dominant, coherent signal is strong enrichment of BAP1 in K4_C0003 (10/20 mutated versus 3/83 in the rest; OR 26.7, 95% CI 6.27-113.5), with significance surviving both driver-panel (q_driver 2.5e-05) and global (q_global 0.0059) correction. PBRM1 shows a nominal depletion trend (4/20 versus 35/83; OR 0.343, p=0.077) that does not survive correction, and VHL prevalence is similar to the rest (13/20 versus 43/83; OR 1.73, p=0.327). The exploratory non-driver genes with nominal enrichment (e.g., RYR3, ARHGEF11) all have q_global = 1.0. The pattern is therefore a focused BAP1-enrichment phenotype rather than a broad mutational signature, and the driver-panel and global multiplicity questions agree for BAP1. Because the rest group is a mixture of the other three candidate sets, this describes how K4_C0003 differs from a composite background rather than from any single alternative set.

The screening therefore returns candidate_k=1, which describes dominance of the single-cluster resolution and does not indicate a dominant internal multi-cluster subdivision. Feasible k>=2 solutions are available (k=2 with children 8/12, k=3 with 5/7/8, k=4 with 4/4/6/6), but their fused-geometry silhouettes are all near zero (0.0007, 0.0006, 0.0004), so none of these feasible internal splits shows meaningful separation. The combination of a dominant single-cluster eigengap and near-zero separation for every feasible k>=2 solution means the internal structure of K4_C0003 is not resolved into distinguishable subclusters in this geometry. This is a set-level structural diagnostic; it does not by itself establish that the set should remain intact or be split, and feasibility of a split is not scientific support for one.

The current set-level structural diagnostic for K4_C0003 is consistent with that partition-level picture: the leading gap is again at the single-cluster resolution, and the feasible k>=2 solutions now reported have near-zero silhouettes. reports.dimension_interpretation: For K4_C0003 (n=20) versus the heterogeneous rest (n=83), the four-view geometry expresses the current membership only weakly. In each modality's native distance geometry the within-label and between-label mean distances are close, and the corresponding silhouettes are small: WSI 0.098, CT 0.069, RNA 0.067, and WXS 0.035. The WXS geometry therefore expresses the K4_C0003 boundary least of the four, while WSI expresses it most, but none of these values indicates a sharply expressed boundary. The global geometry concordance between modality pairs is low to modest (GRV 0.092-0.198), with the strongest shared structure between WSI and RNA and between CT and WSI, and the weakest between CT and RNA and between WSI and WXS. Permutation results indicate that patient correspondence between CT-WSI, RNA-WXS, and WSI-RNA is unlikely under exchangeability, while CT-RNA, WSI-WXS, and CT-WXS are not distinguishable from exchangeable correspondence; these p-values are not action gates. Importantly, the low GRV values do not establish that the views disagree on a boundary, and the modest values do not establish that the views support the same boundary; the tool does not recluster, so these measurements describe geometry similarity and current-label alignment rather than shared subtype boundaries. Taken together, K4_C0003 is weakly separated from the rest in every native modality geometry, and the four views share only limited global patient geometry.
